title: Life, liberty, conviction, education, arrest — Articles 20–22 and 21A

content.overview: Article 20 protects against ex post facto criminal law, double jeopardy, and compelled self-incrimination. Article 21 protects life and personal liberty except according to procedure established by law — after Maneka, that procedure must be fair, just and reasonable. Article 21A guarantees free and compulsory education for children aged six to fourteen as provided by law. Article 22 protects against arrest and detention in certain cases.
content.study: Historical contrast: A.K. Gopalan read Article 21 narrowly. Maneka Gandhi rejected that silo approach and integrated Articles 14, 19 and 21. Current practice: identify the statute, the procedure actually followed, and fairness.

sections.heading: Article 21 after Maneka
sections.body: Procedure established by law must be fair, just and reasonable. Do not treat Article 21 as a free-standing damages statute.

sections.heading: Article 20
sections.body: Three protections: no ex post facto conviction/greater penalty; no double jeopardy; no compelled self-incrimination.
